reference_observations.description: Revisit separate Darwin questions and Mantell answers with the June 5 [1856–1859] thanks. Incoming answers do not become Darwin target voice.

Preserve all 32 paragraphs: observed ant seed stores and sampled loads differ from hypothetical dispersal distances and multiplication. Anthropomorphic committee language is the author’s interpretation.
Keep the incomplete January 1840 body, enclosure, annotations and shelf diagram. Later cosignature is not a same-day receipt witness; the shelf estimate is not precise measurement.

corrections.description: Mixed manuscript: P1/P3 are Darwin questions; P2/P4–6 are Mantell answers. The before-April-10, 1856 bound concerns questions, with answers presumed later. A single early date cannot be applied to all content.

Separate translated De Filippi quotation in P3 from Charles P1/P2/P4. The public note predates October 10, 1862 but was printed January 1863; recent receipt of an 1861 paper does not establish 1861 reading.
Newman’s 1861 response to Darwin 3778 is a later reverse-reply lead. Initiation of fertilisation differs from flying while joined. The specimen box expressly never reached the society.
Preserve the surviving Italian version and its qualified design/creator distinctions. The unseen English original cannot be reconstructed; receipt of an 1869 volume in 1880 is not 1869 knowledge.

summary: Six targets and four contexts reuse matched accepted primary full-source readings. No new current-period edges. Malcolmson’s March 1844 death bounds 559 before this period without resolving its exact date. Mantell 6520 remains a 1856 lead with separately dated questions and answers. Other targets have later contexts; original-language, translated quotation and actual diagram boundaries are retained.
